title: The Inner Citadel: The Meditations of Marcus Aurelius
alternate_titles: La Citadelle intérieure: Introduction aux Pensées de Marc Aurèle

sources.title: La Citadelle intérieure: Introduction aux Pensées de Marc Aurèle
sources.supports: Original French title and subtitle, Pierre Hadot's authorship, publication on 4 November 1992, 386 pages and print ISBN 9782213029849; identifies the work as an introduction to Marcus Aurelius's Meditations and its Stoic practices.
sources.limitations: Authoritative for this French edition's metadata; the description is promotional and does not establish the correctness of Hadot's interpretation. The historical author biography is not a current employment record.

sources.title: The inner citadel: the Meditations of Marcus Aurelius
sources.supports: English title, Pierre Hadot as author, Michael Chase as translator, French original language, Harvard University Press publication in 1998, x plus 351 pages, and ISBNs 0674461711 and 9780674461710; subject headings identify Meditations and Stoicism.
sources.limitations: A bibliographic record, not an independent assessment of the argument. It groups original print and paperback ISBNs, so its 1998 date is used only for the original English edition; the accompanying summary is publisher copy.

sources.title: The Inner Citadel: The Meditations of Marcus Aurelius. Translated by Michael Chase
sources.author_or_publisher: Rachana Kamtekar, Bryn Mawr Classical Review
sources.supports: Directly identifies The Inner Citadel as Hadot's interpretation of Meditations as exercises in philosophical living; explains its treatment of judgement, desire and action and supplies independent grounds for linking the two books.
sources.limitations: One specialist's assessment of the English translation. It also challenges parts of Hadot's account of Stoic doctrine and his limited engagement with alternative interpretations; it supports the connection without settling those disputes.

workflow.coverage_notes: Discovery only: identity, editions and the connection to Meditations checked against publisher and library records and an independent specialist review. No book text has been assessed.
next_steps: Research the book and author when this queue entry is processed, checking Hadot's interpretation against primary Stoic texts and the objections in Kamtekar's review.
